text:
jamie (support): Heads-up — ACME is seeing sustained 429s this morning around 00:10-00:20 UTC. They report bursts of streaming requests and a lot of long-lived connections. stacktrace attached by customer but I pulled server-side counters: 

maria (sre): Can you paste the limiter metrics? TPM/RPM counters and inflight slot usage would help. Also which cluster/region?

jamie (support): cluster: prod-eu-1. From /metrics endpoint (trimmed):
```
rate_limiter.request_count{code="200"} 324512
rate_limiter.request_count{code="429"} 4823
rate_limiter.tpm_window_minutes 1
rate_limiter.tpm_limit 1200
rate_limiter.rpm_limit 6000
rate_limiter.inflight_slots_total 1024
rate_limiter.inflight_slots_used 1018
rate_limiter.streaming_active_connections 412
```

kevin (oncall): inflight_slots_used ~1018 / 1024 is the red flag. :eyes: That means new requests are being queued/dropped even if per-minute counters are below burst thresholds. Are they mostly streaming?

jamie (support): Customer says ~400 concurrent streaming sessions, many send keepalive heartbeats every 15s. They also have an internal fanout that opens short-lived parallel streams for each user action.

devon (platform): Two thoughts: 1) streaming connections hold inflight slots for the whole session; they don't free until connection close. 2) our token-bucket refill is minute-windowed; if many sessions open in quick succession we hit inflight cap first and then 429s even when RPM/TMP look okay. We saw similar with websocket-heavy clients.

maria (sre): Agreed. Can we check the limiter debug log for why we rejected (429 reason codes)? We differentiate: RATE_WINDOW_EXCEEDED vs INFLIGHT_CAP. If it's INFLIGHT_CAP that'll confirm.

rate-limiter-bot: [auto] limiter.reject_reason_counts {"INFLIGHT_CAP": 4118, "RATE_WINDOW_EXCEEDED": 705}

jamie (support): That looks like inflight cap. Customer timeline: spike started 00:06 UTC, peaked 00:12, subsided by 00:22. They pushed a deploy at 23:58 that added a small retry logic in the SDK — could be amplifying open streams.

kevin (oncall): Short term mitigations: 1) Increase inflight_slots_total for prod-eu-1 pool by +256 (fast patch) — watch memory/GC. 2) Advise ACME to reduce keepalive frequency or switch heartbeat aggregation. 3) Add server-side soft-failover: allow short burst of transient slots for streaming for 30s.

devon (platform): I'll prepare a safe ramp: bump to 128 slots now (config change), monitor 5m. If stable, bump further. Also pushing a tweak to prefer closing idle streaming sessions after 300s of inactivity.

maria (sre): For RCA notes: root cause = streaming session churn + new SDK retry behavior causing high concurrent open streams; surface symptom = inflight_slots exhaustion leading to 429s. Action items: 
- revert/adjust SDK retry if they can't reduce sessions (owner: ACME devs)
- platform slot bump + idle timeout (owner: devon)
- add alert for inflight_slots_used > 80% (owner: maria)
- add clearer 429 reason text to API responses so customers see "INFLIGHT_CAP" in body (owner: platform)

jamie (support): Communicated to customer: temporary slot bump and best-effort guidance on SDK heartbeats. They're going to test a client-side change tonight.

kevin (oncall): After we stabilize, let's add a draft KB: "429s from streaming concurrency (inflight cap)" with troubleshooting steps and sample metrics to collect. I'll create a ticket. :+1:

devon (platform): Patch applied: inflight_slots_total=1152 -> effective now. Monitoring: no increase in 5xx or GC. Keeping watch.

maria (sre): Follow-up in 1h for final closure. Thanks all.

jamie (support): Adding timeline and logs to the customer ticket and closing this Slack thread. :white_check_mark:
